newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian shares close weaker, Unibanka dominates.
newsitem.headline: Latvian shares close weaker, Unibanka dominates.

text.p: Latvian shares failed to emerge from their summer torpor by the close on Wednesday, with only good trade in Unibanka keeping the market alive as bourse indices slipped.
Unibanka turned over 67,200 lats, by far the highest of the total market trade of 85,000 lats. Unibanka lost three santimes to 3.27 lats.
The bourse's index slipped to 382.04 from 385.05 while the Rietumu Bank index was down by 0.98 percent to 149.48.

The market has failed to liven up although the bourse has relaxed restrictions on trade sizes, now allowing unlimited trades in shares at the morning price fix session whereas previously the share trade was restricted to a set amount.
But some brokers were positive over the new arrangements, which came into force today.

"This is undoubtedly a positive stimulus to the further development of the market, which will increase interest and brig new investor funds, including from abroad," said Rietumu Bank securities chief Dmitry Krutik in his daily bourse bulletin.

Other dealers were not so sure, saying that investor interest was at a low at the moment given the summer holidays and a lack of new, liquid companies that changes to the trade system will make little difference.
Apart from Unibanka, there was little activity.
Staburadze traded 3,200 lats to fall two santimes to 2.70 lats and Riga Transport Fleet also lost two to 1.27 on 2,100 lats of turnover.
